programs.title: Taste the world with Pascal
programs.desc: This time Pascal will visit a cinnamon plantation.He will be guided through the cultivation by Said, a multi-talented man who can boast of knowing five languages, including Polish.It turns out that cinnamon is dried tree bark.The chef will learn about the healing properties of this plant and the history of the entire island.Ali, Said's father and the village headman, will talk about the beginnings of cinnamon cultivation in Zanzibar and their impact on the functioning of the local community.In addition, Pascal will learn how local houses are built and will try his hand at being a bricklayer.Additionally in the episode: secrets of producing coconut oil and milk from fresh coconuts;schools that were created thanks to crops;making unusual soap and visiting the local market, where you can try traditional wheat pancakes with cinnamon.Pascal himself will prepare pancakes with pineapple, vanilla, coconut flakes and - of course - the flagship spice of Zanzibar.

programs.title: Shocking dishes
programs.desc: This time, Jarosław Nowak's goal is Kazakhstan.It is a country of contrasts, where you can see wild, green steppes and, on the other hand, modern, rapidly developing cities.First, the host visits Almaty, where he tries to discover what Kazakhs consider the strangest delicacy.He sees a traditional slaughterhouse and the world's largest camel farm.His plate includes sheep's head, camel meat and horse meat, which the local population considers to be Kazakh doping.According to culinary tradition and ancient customs, no part of the dish can be wasted, and the preparation of the dish itself is a real celebration.

programs.title: Shocking dishes
programs.desc: Each country has its own traditional dishes.Unusual dishes include:baked bats or bee larvae in honey.Jarosław Nowak gets to know the strangest cuisines in the world.

programs.title: Man, Woman, Wild
programs.desc: In the program, a married couple takes up the challenge and tries to survive in the wilderness.Mykel Hawke is an expert in the US Army Special Forces Survival School, and his wife Ruth is a television journalist.We will meet them in the most remote and dangerous corners of the world, where they will have to survive for four days with only a knife.This is one of the most difficult exams that will test not only their resilience, but also the durability of their marriage in extreme situations.Mykel was taught how to survive in any conditions.However, for Ruth, encounters with wildlife are a completely new experience.A man will have to teach his wife how to build a roof over her head and how to look for food.
